Hi Amelia — appreciated the note and the form. I've attached a short spreadsheet that shows the line-item mapping we typically provide to customers. Quick summary here:

Proposed PO line items (recommended):
1) Redwood Hosted API — Prompt tokens (unit: per 1M tokens) — unit price = $X per 1M prompt tokens
2) Redwood Hosted API — Completion tokens (unit: per 1M tokens) — unit price = $Y per 1M completion tokens
3) Redwood Hosted API — Embeddings (unit: per 1K embeddings) — unit price = $Z per 1K embeddings
4) Redwood Support & Onboarding (unit: monthly) — unit price = $S per month
5) Redwood Reserved Commit (optional) — one-time commit credit (show as credit line)

Notes:
- We present token rates per 1M to keep the unit price readable on POs/invoices rather than per-token micro-pricing.
- Discounts for committed tiers are expressed as a reduced unit price for the relevant bands (e.g., 0–50M, 50–250M, 250M+ per month) and we apply them against billed usage for the invoice period (true-up at invoice).
- If finance needs the vendor form signed, we can fill out the vendor section. Legal will want to review any contract language changes (payment terms, indemnity), but for PO-level administrative fields the form is usually fine.

I've attached Redwood_LineItem_Spreadsheet.xlsx and a short example invoice stub. If you need us to actually populate the PDF form fields, we can do that and return a filled PDF.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm whether GlobalBank requires the unit price to be shown on the face of the vendor form itself or if attaching our spreadsheet alongside the signed form is acceptable?
- Also, please confirm whether GlobalBank's finance needs a monthly invoice or a PO-level prepayment for the committed credit.

Thanks — I looped in Rishi and Priyom for pricing/commit handling.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi/Priyom — quick internal thread before I finalize the filled vendor form:

1) Procurement wants unit prices on PO. Our recommended practice has been to publish per-1M token rates on the invoice and attach a mapping to the PO. Finance sometimes insists on the price being a line-item on the vendor form PDF. Pros/cons?

2) Discount treatment: GlobalBank asked whether discounts are invoice-level true-up vs retroactive. Our standard is invoice-period true-up (we apply the tiered unit price for that invoice period; if they have a committed credit we apply it as a pre-paid credit line). Any reason to consider a different approach for large customers?

3) Does Legal have any issues with putting explicit per-1M token unit prices on the vendor form? Could be perceived as publishing rates; we'd prefer to keep contract pricing in the SOW/quote and show unit prices for PO mapping only.

Please advise and I'll send the filled vendor form (if we can) or return signed+attached spreadsheet.

-J
